label: Use Sequences (Server RBAC role)
type: a Server RBAC role, one of the 56 in learn/security/roles.md. NOT a privilege: Server's concrete role catalogue has no separately enumerable privilege tier, and this token is a role name, not a privilege name. Do NOT confuse with the privilege:capella-advanced-access-* family, which is Capella's genuinely separate 28-member privilege catalogue, nor with capella-role:* (Capella's flat management-plane roles), rbac-role:role, or sgw:role.
note:
Re-filed from privilege: to role: in round 12. roles.md documents this as one of 56 Server RBAC roles, with its own 'Role: <label> (<internal_name>)' table and prose that calls it a role outright. The privilege: id was minted from SQL++ GRANT/REVOKE and monitoring reference pages, which name the bare token without ever classifying it, and round 10 then ruled the reference pages' reading correct - see reconciliation.md round 12. Recurrence 1, promoted under the family exception. Note the label mismatch in the docs' own catalogue: the table header reads 'Role: Manage Sequences' while the internal name is query_use_sequences - see docs-issues/server-role-label-does-not-match-internal-name. Promoted as part of the nine-member query_* role family rather than on its own recurrence. The family exception applies for an unusual reason worth stating: the misclassification is contagious through the extraction layer. An agent reusing privilege:query-delete and truthfully declaring it extraction-layer passes the write-time gate, so the wrong id keeps spreading with no diagnostic. A promoted role: record that aliases the privilege: form converts that silent reuse into a gate denial. Promotion here is the control point, not a claim that one page is enough evidence.

ROUND 13 LABEL CORRECTION. This record was promoted with the label 'Manage Sequences', because that is what roles.md's table says: the section headed 'Use Sequences' carries the table header 'Role: Manage Sequences (query_use_sequences)', a label copy-pasted from the preceding role. The internal name is correct and the heading is correct; only the table label is wrong. The `evidence` field below still quotes it verbatim, because that is genuinely what the page says.

This is the cleanest example in the corpus of why a passing evidence gate is not a passing record. The quote is real, the gate allowed it, verify-evidence.py still allows it, and the record was wrong - because the defect was in the source document, and a checker that compares a record against the page cannot catch a page that contradicts itself. Round 12 also saw this table and recorded it as a label-vs-internal-name naming inconsistency (docs-issues/server-role-label-does-not-match-internal-name), which inverted the diagnosis: query_use_sequences is not an odd internal name for Manage Sequences, it is the right internal name for Use Sequences under a mislabelled header. See docs-issues/roles-md-use-sequences-table-mislabelled.
